To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conserved arginine of box II is essential for the in vivo recombination activity of IntI1, whereas the conserved arginines of box I are not required for the recombination activity but are required for substrate binding.
the three residues in the conserved boxes of IntI1 are important for substrate recognition and recombination, but only one residue is required for the catalytic activity of the recombinase.

mutations at the invariant tyrosine residue of the IntI1 protein affect its recombination capacity, but not substrate recognition; the mutation of the box II invariant arginine affects both substrate binding and recombination, but the efficiency of these processes is lower than that of the wild type; and the mutation of the conserved residue of the box I region has no effect on recombination, but substrate binding is affected.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the role of these conserved residues in the catalytic properties of the IntI1 integrase.
the analysis of point mutations in the integron integrase IntI1, which affects recombination and/or substrate recognition.
the characterization of the properties of the site-specific recombinases IntI1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three conserved amino acids of the family are required for the in vitro and in vivo functions of IntI1.
the three conserved amino acids are important for IntI1-mediated recombination, but only the box II arginines are essential.
the conserved arginine in box II (R280) is the most important for the function of IntI1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three invariant residues of the tyrosin recombinase family are essential for the catalytic activity of the integrase IntI1.

the conserved residues in box I (Arg-146) and in box II (Arg-280) are important for both substrate recognition and recombination, while the tyrosine (Tyr-312) in box II is only important for recombination.

the three conserved amino acids are important for the recombination and substrate binding of IntI1, although the box II arginines and the tyrosine are more crucial for the recombination than the box I arginine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the three conserved amino acid residues are important for substrate recognition and/or recombination, but the box I arginine is not essential.
the tyrosine and box II arginine are required for the catalytic activity, whereas the box I arginine is not essential for the catalytic function but is important for the substrate recognition.
IntI1 is more flexible than the other tyrosine recombinations in its requirements for the conserved residues of box I and box III.
